newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open down 5.00 to 8.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open down 5.00 to 8.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open down 5.00 to 8.00 cents Wednesday on news that Colombia opened "unlimited" coffee registrations, traders said.

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said late Tuesday Colombia was opening "unlimited" coffee registrations for July-August, a period in which he said the country was expected to export 2.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee.

Ocampo said that registrations opening Wednesday morning for the two-month period would be "without restrictions," meaning that private exporters, and the Colombian National Growers' Federation were authorized to export all the coffee they could get their hands on.
But Ocampo said that no more than 2.5 million bags would be available for shipment, adding that "it's not a lot of coffee."

Tuesday, New York arabica futures rose sharply in seesaw trading, lifted by a late bout of commercial buying. July ended up 10.25 cents at 264.20 cents a lb after ranging between 268.50 and 249.00. September ended 8.50 cents higher at 233.05 cents, while the back months finished up 8.10 to down 2.00.
The July/September spread widened to 31.15 cents from 29.40 cents at the close on Monday. September/December stretched to 36.00 cents from 35.60 cents.
Technically, traders said July would find support at Monday's low of 247.50, while resistance was seen at 275.00.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 2,250 60-kg bags as of June 2, to 45,985 bags, There were 1,320 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Weather Services Corp. said on Wednesday no damaging cold weather was expected to hit Brazil's coffee belt this weekend, although temperatures could turn colder. However, the situation bears watching, WSC said.

London robusta futures slumped early Wednesday, after a firm start, pressured by origin selling and the Colombian news. LIFFE July was down $22 at the midday break, to $2,138, after peaking at $2,240.
